issues.description: The netlist as shipped is malformed/inconsistent with the intended ground truth. It contains leftover draft artifacts (references to c_bugged, n_o0_bugged macros in comments/dead text causing iverilog warnings) and the actual wiring of u_perm_nand3 uses .c(n_o0_qual) fed through a NOR2/INV correction cone (u_nor_o0_qual, u_inv_o0_qual, u_nand_corr, u_inv_corr) rather than a clean single-instance bug. This causes the flip-sensitivity analysis in evaluate.py to implicate 13+ extra instances (u_inv_a0, u_inv_corr, u_inv_o0_qual, u_inv_o1, u_inv_out, u_inv_owner_qual, u_inv_req10, u_inv_t3, u_nand_corr, u_nand_req10, u_nand_t3, u_nor_o0_qual, u_nor_out) as ground-truth suspects instead of the intended sole {u_perm_nand3}, per the differential report's golden_rejected failure.
issues.evidence: differential.golden_run.stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: SR3: suspect_instances is missing ground-truth-implicated instance(s): ["u_inv_a0", "u_inv_corr", ... 13 instances]' despite golden submitting exactly {u_perm_nand3} as the correct answer per hidden_spec.ground_truth.

issues.description: The grader's golden run rejects the expert/golden solution (exit 1, SR3 FAIL) when it should pass (exit 0). This directly violates the submission contract requirement that a correct submission must be accepted.
issues.evidence: differential.golden_run: {'exit_code':1,'expected':'pass','ok':false,'status':'fail', stdout shows 'PASS: SR1','PASS: SR2', but 'FAIL: SR3' with a long list of unintended flip-sensitive instances.

issues.description: The Verilog file contains stray/incomplete draft reasoning text with backtick-fenced code blocks and undefined macro references (c_bugged, n_o0_bugged) embedded as comments before the real module, causing iverilog compile warnings. This is leftover scratch content that should not ship in a participant-facing input artifact.
issues.evidence: Golden run stderr: '[INFO] iverilog cross-check compile failed (non-fatal): inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v:25: warning: macro c_bugged undefined...' plus the file content shows a long prose/JSON/markdown preamble before the actual 'timescale' and module declaration.

issues.description: mutation_score is 0.0 and mutation_status is blocked_by_differential; requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0, meaning no security mutants were actually validated as detectable because the differential check failed at the golden-acceptance stage before mutation testing could proceed.

The manifest/purpose text for perm_cone_netlist.v explicitly describes the intended single-instance bug mechanics in detail (which port swapped, which gate to isolate), which is scratch/internal generation metadata rather than participant-facing content, but since it appears in the bundle's manifest (not the actual README/design_brief shown to participants) this is lower severity; however the actual shipped .v file itself contains verbose exploratory reasoning about the bug design that goes beyond what a real synthesis artifact would contain.
issues.evidence: inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v file content includes multi-paragraph first-person reasoning ('Let me verify the logic before writing... I need a wiring bug that only breaks 101 without breaking 100...') directly inside the artifact delivered to participants.

recommendations: Fix inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v to contain only the clean, final Verilog module — strip all the leftover draft/reasoning prose, backtick code fences, and undefined macro references (c_bugged, n_o0_bugged) that currently precede the actual module declaration and leak the hidden bug design to participants.

Regenerate the netlist so the flip-sensitivity analysis in evaluate.py resolves the ground-truth suspect set to exactly {u_perm_nand3} as intended, rather than 13+ additional instances (u_inv_a0, u_nor_out, u_inv_out, etc.). This likely requires restructuring the correction sub-cone so it is truly gate-count-minimal and does not create alternate flip-equivalent paths through T1/T2 merge and final-stage gates.

Re-run the differential test after the netlist fix to confirm the golden solution (submitting {u_perm_nand3} and the single diverging vector) achieves exit code 0 with all SR1-SR4 and FR1-FR4 marked PASS.
Once golden acceptance is fixed, re-run mutation testing, since mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score are currently 0.0 and meaningless due to the blocked differential check.

Consider tightening SR3 grading logic (or the netlist topology) so that the flip-sensitivity heuristic is robust to intermediate inverter/buffer stages that trivially propagate the flip without independent causal significance, to avoid over-broad suspect sets in future revisions.
Review all input artifacts for any remaining scratch/generation-time text before shipping; the current perm_cone_netlist.v is unsuitable for participant consumption in its present state.
